correctness.rationale: For A chosen attribute vertices and D=V\A, each selected edge of a reduced contranominal subcontext contains exactly one chosen vertex and its other endpoint lies in D. The missing-incidence bijection requires one distinct cross-edge for each v in A, giving precisely product_{v in A}|N(v) intersect D|; nonzero iff D dominates G, including isolates and n=1, hence top degree n-gamma(G). The established FCA scale criterion supplies an ORDER embedding, not a sublattice statement. The star equality count follows by enumerating closed intents; adding any non-spoke edge produces an additional closed intent containing the hub. For path/cycle, the four-state transition weights z(a+c) at a zero center and 1 at a one center, with appropriate boundary vectors, recover the recurrence and floor(2n/3) degree. Cut-edge expectations factor over v in A since those Bernoulli sets are disjoint. Independently constructed all 75 labeled graph edge-subsets n<=4, and compared direct edge-subcontext enumeration to the product formula exactly, plus direct sample transfer polynomials. The source verify.py additionally implements 1099 graph checks through order five; its log alone was not treated as proof.

value.rationale: The complementary edge-vertex context is a natural formal-concept representation of a graph, and domination number is a central graph invariant. This identifies Boolean suborder rank exactly and lifts existence to every weighted scale coefficient, enabling exact graph-family recurrences and testing sharpness of a natural concept-count bound. It is not merely restating NP-completeness or the known generic FCA scale theorem; the unknown weighted polynomial and equality structure have independent mathematical use.
